nationalKeyInfo.title: Value-based procurement is the national standard
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The DHSC / NHS England / NHS Supply Chain national standard scores medtech tenders on wider value (social value, efficiency, patient & staff, supply chain, purpose) weighted ≥60%, with whole-life cost capped at 40%. Procurement must save money AND show value.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Frame every case as value, not price. Build it in the Value Case Calculator and hand procurement a figure they can take to finance.

nationalKeyInfo.title: New NHS Supply Chain online catalogue
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A new online catalogue and search rolled out from late 2025 (search by NPC, MPC, supplier, brand, GTIN or free text).
nationalKeyInfo.use: A genuine, non-salesy opener: “how are you finding the new catalogue?”

nationalKeyInfo.title: New Hospital Programme reset
nationalKeyInfo.detail: Reset in Jan 2025 into delivery Waves 0–3; costed ~£56bn (NAO, Jan 2026). RAAC-affected trusts are prioritised in Wave 1.
nationalKeyInfo.use: If your trust has a new build, get in at design stage — equipment is specified 12–24 months before it opens.

nationalKeyInfo.title: Carbon scored at tender (Evergreen)
nationalKeyInfo.detail: NHS Supply Chain requires Evergreen Level 1 (a Carbon Reduction Plan + net-zero commitment) at tender close from 6 April 2026.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Have your carbon and sustainability position ready — it is scored, not optional.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NIHR HealthTech Research Centres — the NHS route to your own evidence
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A network of NIHR-funded centres of excellence hosted inside NHS trusts across England, set up specifically to help medical device, diagnostic, IVD and digital companies develop, evaluate and validate health technologies. They support real-world evidence generation and health economics, so a supplier can build NHS evidence with an NHS partner rather than arriving with vendor data alone. Each centre has its own clinical focus.
nationalKeyInfo.use: The answer when a trust says 'show me it works here'. If your evidence is manufacturer-run or from another health system, this is a named, credible route to NHS-generated proof — and raising it marks you out as someone who understands how the NHS actually accepts new technology.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NHS Supply Chain has a clinical assurance gate, not just a commercial one
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The Clinical and Product Assurance function (CaPA) sits inside NHS Supply Chain. Registered clinicians — nurses, midwives and allied health professionals — work across its clinical, commercial, customer engagement and strategy directorates to make sure the medical devices, products and consumables it sources meet NHS standards of safety, quality and effectiveness. Clinical judgement sits inside the sourcing process itself, not only at the trust that eventually buys.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Stop treating a framework as a purely commercial decision. Clinical evidence, usability and patient-safety arguments carry weight inside NHS Supply Chain's own sourcing process, not just with your trust. Ask how the clinical assurance for your category was done and what it looked at.

trusts.name: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: Queen's Hospital in Romford and King George Hospital in Goodmayes, serving one of the fastest-growing populations in England. Financially this is a turnaround account: a reported deficit of £30.7m in 2024/25 sitting on an underlying deficit of £46m, with an adjusted financial performance deficit of £38.9m against £6.1m the year before. The recovery plan requires savings of £61m, equal to 6% of income. Leadership is unusually thin on permanence — Chief Executive, Chief Operating Officer and Chief People Officer are all interim as at 14/08/2026 — so expect decisions to take longer and large commitments to need more cover than usual.
trusts.news: The Board has a Finance, Investment and Performance Committee scrutinising delivery of the financial recovery plan and savings programme, chaired by Sue Lees. The trust's own recovery narrative names right-sizing medical staffing and slippage in medical premium savings as the problems to fix, and commits to “further efficiency programmes to maintain and ensure high function performance across all core theatre capacity”. Board papers for 2026/27 are published four days before each meeting but the trust's document library does not expose them directly, so the current-year financial position could not be verified here — the £61m figure is the plan set out in the 2024/25 annual report.
trusts.structure: Payment performance has deteriorated sharply and it matters if you are carrying stock: 83.1% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume in 2024/25, down from 91.5% the year before, and 87.4% by value against 96.2%. That is the largest single-year fall in payment performance of any trust profiled in the Hub, and it is consistent with a trust managing cash through a deficit. Spend over £30,000 is published monthly. The Finance, Investment and Performance Committee is the body scrutinising the savings programme, so proposals framed as recovery-plan contributions have a named audience. Not verified: the size and structure of the procurement team, the e-tendering portal used, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published on the trust's site.

trusts.name: Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A two-site trust formed by the 2020 merger of Luton and Dunstable University Hospital and Bedford Hospital, around 9,000 staff, in NHS oversight segment 3. The access position is difficult — 82,592 on the waiting list, 59.1% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 14.6 weeks and 731 people over 52 weeks. Financially it runs at the line: an adjusted financial performance surplus of £415k in 2024/25 on operating expenses of £908m, with the statutory deficit driven by the impairment of new buildings brought into use during the year. The trust has a named turnaround function that has already gone after theatre and outpatient productivity, and it says non-pay cost is the focus area for 2025/26 — which is precisely where a supplier proposition lands.
trusts.news: Pippa Nightingale has taken over as Chief Executive, arriving from London North West University Healthcare where she led the trust out of special measures and delivered financial breakeven across three acute sites; her background is as a registered midwife and she was awarded an MBE for services to nursing and midwifery leadership. The trust's Financial Turnaround Team identified 66 schemes worth £23.6m, covering theatre productivity, outpatient productivity, reducing out-of-hours operating and demand management in pathology and imaging — and the trust makes a point of having done it “on sustainable improvements rather than using external consultants”. That work has become a Strategic Financial Planning programme with a named lead. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: Procurement is held directly by the Director of Finance. Matt Gibbons's published board responsibilities are Finance, Financial Management, Procurement and Sustainability Champion — so finance, buying and the sustainability agenda sit with one person, and a case that covers all three at once is talking to a single owner. He has been in post since October 2019 and joined the organisation in 2002, so expect deep familiarity with the existing supplier base. Clinical Directors are a joint responsibility of the Medical Director and the Deputy Chief Executive, and the Medical Director, Mr Paul Tisi, explicitly owns GIRFT — a vascular and general surgeon by background, which matters if you sell into vascular or general surgery. Cathy Jones as Deputy Chief Executive holds clinical service lines, operational management, performance and business development. One stated gap worth knowing: the trust reports “a lack of a unified Electronic Patient Record system across sites” and limited interoperability with external partners, which shapes any digital or data-dependent proposition. Board correspondence goes through Victoria Parsons, Associate Director of Corporate Governance and Company Secretary, at Nova House, Luton and Dunstable University Hospital. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.

trusts.name: Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A community trust, so it files no consultant-led RTT return and carries no acute oversight segment — the data panel above will be thinner than for an acute trust, and that is correct rather than missing. Its own waiting position is comparatively good: 80.2% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 8.7 weeks and nobody over 52 weeks on a 14,961 list. The single most important fact about selling here is that BCHC does not run its own procurement. It receives procurement support on a shared basis from the BSol Procurement Collaborative, hosted by University Hospitals Birmingham, which buys for five trusts across the whole Birmingham and Solihull ICS. Win the category at BSol and you have addressed five organisations; lose it and BCHC is not a separate route back in.
trusts.news: BCHC reported a £2.6m surplus on the adjusted control-total basis for 2024/25 against a statutory deficit of £1.7m, but its cost improvement programme under-delivered — 84.5% of the year-to-date plan against a 95% target — while the capital programme over-delivered at 96.87% against a 90% target. External auditor Mazars identified no significant weaknesses in the trust's arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published on the trust's site when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated here.
trusts.structure: Procurement is delivered by the BSol Procurement Collaborative, hosted by University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust and serving UHB, Birmingham Women's and Children's, the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, Birmingham Community Healthcare and Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health — one of the first procurement teams in the country to work across an entire ICS, and winner of the HCSA 2023 Procurement and Supply Chain Team of the Year. It is led by Simon Clarke, Managing Director, whose senior management team reports into a quarterly Partnership Board and chairs the BSol Procurement Collaborative Operational Delivery Group. It holds a 'Good' CCIAF accreditation. The team is published in five parts, each with its own generic inbox, so a supplier can address the right function directly: Strategic Procurement (BSOLCategoryTeams@uhb.nhs.uk), which agrees CIP targets with finance leads, writes strategic sourcing documents for major projects and produces contract award reports; the Clinical Procurement Specialist team (ProcurementCPSTeam@uhb.nhs.uk), clinical experts reporting to a Head of Clinical Procurement who source alternatives during stockouts and national shortages and drive standardisation across the ICS; Data Analytics, Catalogue and Systems (ProcurementData@uhb.nhs.uk), which owns the BSol Master Products Catalogue — the route to getting a product code listed; Transactional Procurement (BSOLProcurementBuyers@uhb.nhs.uk), with set buyers per trust across six different ordering systems; and Pharmacy Procurement (Pharmacy.Procurement@uhb.nhs.uk). The Collaborative is based at 1 Regent Court, George Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham B15 1NU. Contracts are awarded in compliance with procurement law, trust standing financial instructions and the scheme of delegation. Not verified: whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published by BCHC or the Collaborative, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.

trusts.name: Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A mid-sized teaching trust serving around 667,000 people across seven sites, in NHS oversight segment 3, with a comparatively contained access position — 69.3% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 10.9 weeks and 55 people over 52 weeks on a 31,604 list. It beat its financial plan in 2024/25, closing a £4.9m deficit against a planned £9.7m, but the year ahead is much harder: a projected £17m deficit for 2025/26 requiring £33m of productivity savings. The opening is capital rather than revenue — three named new-build schemes are in flight, and all three are directly relevant to devices and consumables.
trusts.news: The trust names three new capital developments as live opportunities to improve services: a new Community Diagnostic Centre, a dedicated day case unit at St Luke's Hospital, and a new endoscopy suite. Financial governance runs through a programme the trust calls 'Closing the Gap', alongside development of an Estates Strategy and prioritisation of backlog maintenance. Internal audit during the year covered Estates Procurement (BH48 2024) and Procurement and Business Cases (BH25 2025), so procurement process is under active internal scrutiny. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: Procurement is unambiguously a finance function here. The trust's own table of executive directors' key responsibilities puts Finance, Procurement, Contracting and Capital all under the Chief Finance Officer — so the CFO is the accountable owner of a buying decision, not a distant approver, and a business case that reads as a finance case will travel further than one that reads as a clinical wish. Estates, the Capital Programme, Clinical Engineering and Sustainability sit together under the Director of Estates and Facilities, which is the route for equipment, maintenance and backlog cases. The trust also works with West Yorkshire partners on joint projects spanning procurement, so check whether a category is bought at West Yorkshire level before assuming it is a Bradford decision. One observable quirk worth knowing: five of the seventeen Bradford buyer contacts in the Hub's own contacts data were named on notices whose title begins 'Waiver' — single-tender waivers published as award notices — and no other trust in this batch shows any. That is counted over published notice titles only, and it is a signal about how contracts here get published, not proof of how they get awarded. Not verified: no e-tendering portal, procurement team structure or supplier representative booking system is confirmed — the trust's public website is behind bot protection and could not be read directly, so none of this could be checked on the live site.

trusts.name: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Ipswich and Colchester hospitals plus community services across east Suffolk and north Essex. The 2024/25 accounts show a £38.6m deficit, but £43.8m of that is a non-cash asset impairment — on the control total NHS England actually judges them on, they delivered a £3.5m surplus against a £0.25m target. So this is not a trust in crisis; it is one that hit its number. The softer spot is the quality of its savings: £22.7m delivered but only £12.7m of it recurrent, and the auditors identified weaknesses in how cost improvement delivery is tracked. Both executive leadership posts a supplier cares about — Chief Executive and Chief Finance Officer — are held on an interim basis as at 14/08/2026, so major commitments may move slowly.
trusts.news: Two surgical hubs are the story for anyone selling into theatres: a dedicated elective orthopaedic centre with its own theatres, three wards and 72 inpatient beds, and a surgical hub at Ipswich opened July 2024 with three specialist theatres and a same-day admissions ward covering general surgery, ENT, oral surgery and urology. The Clacton Site Transformation and Redevelopment (STAR) will significantly increase diagnostics activity. Board papers for 2026/27 are published but the trust's document library does not expose the finance report directly — the current-year position is therefore not verified here.
trusts.structure: A trust that has put social value and local supply at the centre of how it buys, and says so in its own annual report: it is a member of the Suffolk and North East Essex ICB Procurement Anchor Group, states that it buys locally wherever possible from small and medium sized businesses, and in its soft facilities management tender required bidders to state how and to what extent they would achieve social value and sustainability objectives. If you have a Carbon Reduction Plan and a local supply or employment story, lead with it here — it is scored, not decorative. Contracts are published on the trust's own contract register and all spend over £25,000 is published monthly. Payment is reasonable: 77.8% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume and 89.8% by value in 2024/25. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute trusts in England — QMC, City Hospital and Ropewalk House — and financially the hardest-pressed trust in this batch. 2025/26 closed £12.2m in deficit against a breakeven plan, having delivered £67.6m of a £97.7m efficiency target. 2026/27 asks for £106m of savings and the Board has already been told the level of ambition must increase. The Board's own view is that the cost base is unsustainable relative to income, so this is not a trust looking for nice-to-haves: bring a cash-releasing number or expect a short meeting. Their estate cannot rescue them either — the Tomorrow's NUH rebuild is postponed to 2037 at the earliest and they carry the fourth largest maintenance backlog in the country.
trusts.news: Month 2 (May 2026) reported to the public Board on 09/07/2026: £23.0m year-to-date deficit, £6.1m adverse to plan, with a £4.5m year-to-date overspend on clinical supplies and services driven by higher-than-planned activity. Efficiency delivery £6.3m against a £7.1m year-to-date plan. A “Plan B” is being worked up for the parts of Tomorrow's NUH that cannot wait until 2037, with backlog maintenance named as a main priority. The National Rehabilitation Centre, a 70-bed purpose-built NHS facility near Loughborough and the first of its kind in the UK, is staffed and run by NUH and due to open.
trusts.structure: NUH operates a strict “no purchase order, no payment” policy — an invoice without an official PO number, and not on the exception list, is rejected outright. The PO is issued before you start supplying and is emailed to the address held in your supplier record, so get your supplier details right before anything ships. Invoices go to NHS Shared Business Services, not to the trust; accountspayable@nuh.nhs.uk handles disputes. They aim to pay within 30 days and frequently do not: in 2024/25 only 59.9% of non-NHS invoices were paid on time by volume and 58.4% by value, so price your working capital accordingly. Contracts over £25k are published on Contracts Finder. The distinctive route in for a device company is CHEATA — the Centre for Healthcare Equipment and Technology Adoption, a contract-based service embedded in the trust's Clinical Engineering department offering value propositions, health economic analysis, evidence gathering, NICE engagement and regulatory advice to manufacturers at any stage. Contacts Dr Sarah Bolton (Business Manager) and Sinead Barker (Programme Co-ordinator), nuhnt.cheata@nhs.net. Not verified whether NUH runs a separate rep booking or accreditation system for ward and theatre access.

trusts.name: Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A mental health, learning disability and community trust, so it files no consultant-led RTT return and carries no acute oversight segment — the data panel above will be thin, and that is correct rather than missing. It is nonetheless a substantial commercial organisation: turnover rose £66m to £693m in 2024/25, it holds £97.8m of cash, which it describes as one of the strongest positions in its local area, and it increased capital investment to £24.5m. Two things make it unusual. It is lead provider for three NHS provider collaboratives — forensic inpatient mental health, CAMHS Tier 4 and adult eating disorders — holding the budgets and commissioner responsibilities for those specialised services, so it buys as a commissioner as well as a provider. And it runs the Oxford Pharmacy Store, a trading service that grew by £28m in the year.
trusts.news: The Warneford Park programme is the big one: a redevelopment of the Warneford Hospital site in Headington, taken forward through a joint vehicle, Warneford Park LLP, with pre-planning application consultations launched in August 2024. The accounts record a contingent liability capped at £4,175k — if the trust does not proceed once planning permission is achieved and funding identified, it must reimburse in full the jointly incurred planning and preparatory costs. Alongside it, a new Jordan Hill Community Health Hub in North Oxford took £5.2m of estates capital in 2024/25. The trust targets net zero carbon by 2045 and has a revised Green Plan. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: Commercial leadership sits with the Chief Finance Officer, Heather Smith, and her portfolio is unusually wide: the trust states she is responsible for the financial and commercial leadership of the trust and also for the Information Management & Technology and Estates & Facilities teams, and that she is senior responsible officer for the Warneford Park programme. She came from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, where she was also Chief Finance Officer, with earlier senior civil service finance roles at HMRC, BIS and HM Treasury — expect a public-sector business-case discipline rather than an NHS-only frame of reference. trusts.name: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A £1.76bn teaching trust across the Royal Hallamshire, Northern General, Weston Park, Charles Clifford and Jessop Wing, and one of the few in this batch that is genuinely in surplus — £6.93m, 0.4% of turnover, on turnover up 11.5%. That makes it a different sell from the turnaround trusts: they are not desperate, so a pure price argument carries less weight, and the trust says plainly that 2025/26 brings “an even more constrained financial position”. Their stated approach is driving out unnecessary variation rather than blanket cuts, which favours suppliers who can evidence standardisation and reduced variation over those offering a discount.
trusts.news: Clinical supplies spend rose more than a fifth in a year, to £164.3m. The trust has almost eliminated the longest waits for treatment while its waiting list grew 0.7%. Its stated priorities for the year are “driving out unnecessary variation, refining our ways of working and through partnerships explore how we deliver the best value for the resources we are given”, navigated as a partner in the wider South Yorkshire system rather than alone.
trusts.structure: Two published procurement commitments are directly actionable for a supplier. First, social value is a part of all competitive procurements and environmental considerations are built into procurement processes — so it is scored, not decorative. Second, and more unusually, the procurement teams are explicitly working to increase the use of local businesses and suppliers specifically to reduce the road miles in their supply chain and support the local economy. If you have a Yorkshire or northern distribution point, warehouse or manufacturing site, that is a scoring argument here and not merely a nice story — quantify the road miles saved. Note the trust runs two Chief Medical Officers, split into Development and Operations, so the right clinical sponsor depends on whether you are proposing a new service or improving an existing one. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, the procurement team's size, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: Do not sell to this trust as a standalone organisation. ULTH and Lincolnshire Community Health Services NHS Trust operate as the Lincolnshire Community and Hospitals NHS Group, and the Group Board is “the joint board and decision-making body for both statutory organisations” — a single set of group executives covers finance, operations, estates and clinical governance across both. It sits in NHS oversight segment 4 and stayed there at the Quarter 4 2025/26 ratings published in June 2026, with a 70,206 waiting list, 61.9% within 18 weeks and 1,113 people over 52 weeks. The commercial picture is not simply distress, though: the trust over-delivered its savings plan in 2024/25 and fully spent an £88.1m capital programme, and has an unusually visible pipeline of new-build diagnostic and theatre capacity.
trusts.news: The Group Board meeting of 07/07/2026 reported an £8.1m deficit at month two, in line with plan, and confirmed ULTH remained in oversight segment 4 at the Quarter 4 National Oversight Framework ratings while LCHS dropped from segment 2 to 3. The ULTH Electronic Patient Record implementation is “continuing at pace”, with first go-live scheduled for October 2026 and parallel digitisation of existing paper records. The Lincolnshire Community Diagnostic Centre programme now runs CDCs at Grantham, Skegness and Lincoln with a fourth being built at Boston. The Lincolnshire system formally exited Urgent and Emergency Care Tier 2 oversight in May 2026. Implementation of the new Patient Services Hub has been temporarily paused while problems are worked through. The 2025/26 annual report and accounts had been submitted but not yet published when this profile was written.
trusts.structure: Buying decisions sit at group level, not trust level — approach Lincolnshire Community and Hospitals NHS Group, and expect a proposition to be tested against both an acute and a community trust. Group Chief Finance Officer Paul Antunes Goncalves came from 16 years at Nottingham University Hospitals, most recently as Director of Finance, so he will already know the supplier base of a large Midlands teaching trust. Capital is governed through a Capital Delivery Group reporting to the Finance, Performance and Estates Committee, with quarterly reporting, and the capital prioritisation process is informed by the six-facet estate survey — a backlog-maintenance case has a defined route here. Estates is the standout capital relationship: Group Chief Estates and Facilities Officer Mike Parkhill has run the largest capital programme in the trust's history, covering the Lincoln County emergency department, urgent treatment centre and respiratory support unit, new theatres at Grantham, the Grantham CDC, the new Pilgrim emergency department and the Lincoln and Skegness CDCs. But read the outlook before assuming an easy year: the trust calls 2026/27 “extremely challenging” and faces a recurrent savings requirement of £92.6m to break even, which it describes as “an unprecedented level of challenge”. Its commissioner also changed on 01/04/2026, when North Central London ICB merged with North West London to form West and North London ICB.
trusts.news: UCLH was chosen by the Department of Health and Social Care as the launch site for its programme to cut reliance on single-use items, with the minister shown reusable and remanufactured theatre products in a mock theatre on site — reusables, remanufacture and Design for Life are live procurement priorities here, not aspirations. The trust is also leading the procurement and commissioning of a PACS shared in common across North Central London hospitals, and a national first-in-type scheme integrating Epic with the national e-prescription service, due to let patients collect UCLH prescriptions from community pharmacies in 2027.
trusts.structure: Procurement sits under Tim Jaggard, deputy chief executive and chief financial officer, who signed the 2025/26 accounts on 25/06/2026. Sustainability is an explicit and published part of buying decisions: the trust commits to “ensure sustainability forms a greater part of our procurement decision-making”, to “meet or exceed NHS England's procurement roadmap”, to increase reuse and remanufacture while reducing single-use, and to engage suppliers to pilot more sustainable items. Supply-chain emissions are the largest part of a 202,818 tCO₂e carbon footprint, with net zero for indirect and supply-chain emissions targeted by 2040. The trust uses NHS Terms and Conditions and weighs modern slavery factors in procurement decisions. It pays well by NHS standards — 91% of invoices by volume and 96% by value paid to terms in 2025/26. Several large buys run at North Central London level rather than trust level, PACS being the current example, so check whether your category is bought by UCLH alone before targeting it. Not verified: whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — UCLH publishes no supplier representatives policy and no e-tendering portal of its own on its public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one. trusts.name: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Four hospitals — Queen Elizabeth Birmingham, Heartlands, Good Hope and Solihull — and one of the largest trusts in England. Financially it is under formal NHS England scrutiny: the trust reported an overall deficit of £69.5m in 2024/25 and, on the adjusted measure NHS England judges it on, a £0.9m surplus reached only after a Financial Recovery Plan agreed in September 2024 in response to an £81.4m adjusted deficit at month eight. It is rated 4 — Investigation and Intervention — under the NHSE Rapid Intervention process. The savings that got them there do not repeat: over half were non-recurrent, so the same gap reopens each year. A trust that needs recurrent, provable savings, not one-offs.

No 2026/27 board papers were publicly locatable on the trust's website as at 14/08/2026 — unlike Leeds and Nottingham, UHB does not publish an accessible board pack archive, so the current-year position here is not verified. Payment performance is mid-range: 76.9% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume, 73.4% by value in 2024/25. trusts.context: Seven hospitals and community services across Sussex, close to 20,000 staff. It carries the hardest access position in this batch — 116,122 on the waiting list, only 53.2% within 18 weeks and 4,636 people waiting over 52 weeks — and sits in NHS oversight segment 4, the tier requiring mandated support. 2025/26 closed at a £4.9m surplus on the control-total basis agreed with Sussex ICB, but the trust delivered only £96.8m of a £109m efficiency target. trusts.context: One of the largest acute trusts in the country and, on the numbers, one of the hardest-pressed in this batch: 115,259 on the waiting list, 60.1% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 14.0 weeks, 2,402 people over 52 weeks, and NHS oversight segment 4. trusts.name: University Hospitals of North Midlands NHS Trust
trusts.context: A £1.29bn-income trust across Royal Stoke University Hospital and County Hospital in Stafford, with around 1,450 inpatient beds, in NHS oversight segment 3. The access position is mid-table for this batch — 72,002 waiting, 63.0% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 13.1 weeks, 1,360 people over 52 weeks. The fact that shapes every commercial conversation here is the Section 30 referral: because of a cumulative deficit, the trust's external auditors referred it to the Secretary of State for Health in June 2021, and that referral was still in place through 2024/25. Expect scrutiny of any spend, and expect recurrent savings to be valued far above one-off ones — the trust says its 2024/25 position “relied heavily on non-recurrent cost improvement scheme delivery and other one-off benefits”.
trusts.news: The trust ended 2024/25 with an £11.8m deficit against a breakeven plan and has appointed a Recovery Director alongside a revised Urgent and Emergency Care improvement programme. Its County Elective Hub has significantly increased procedure numbers, with day case activity running at 107.4% of plan — the elective hub is the growth point. On the supply side, the Procurement Team's Energy Procurement Partnership with Stoke-on-Trent City Council cut a potential £10m cost pressure to around £3m and has been extended for a further two years, and the second and final phase of the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme put £3m into air source heat pumps, LED lighting and solar at Royal Stoke as part of a £5.4m programme. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: The most useful thing to know about this procurement team is that it co-develops products with suppliers rather than only buying them. Its published example is the Eco Box, developed jointly with the trust's anti-embolism stockings supplier: they removed the dye to save energy, water and chemicals, stripped the plastic packaging, trialled it on wards, and then adapted the format again after patients said they preferred individually wrapped take-home packs — projected saving 7.8 tonnes of plastic and 10 tonnes of cardboard a year. A supplier arriving with a sustainability redesign proposal has a proven precedent to point at. Procurement also sits inside the monthly Sustainability Working Group structure, and the team runs supplier awareness work on Modern Slavery Act compliance as part of onboarding new suppliers, so expect that check when trading for the first time. Financial performance, cost improvement schemes and capital schemes are all standing monthly items at the non-executive-led Performance and Finance Committee, which is where a large business case will be seen. Estates, Facilities and PFI are held together by one director, and the trust describes “exemplar relationships” with its PFI partners. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.
